tagline: Chatbots, chips and the trillion-dollar race everyone has an opinion on.
why: Artificial intelligence went from a research topic to everyday life when ChatGPT launched in late 2022. Now it's in workplaces, phones and the stock market, and everyone talks about which tools they use, whether AI will take jobs, and how fast it's improving. You don't need to be technical; knowing the key players, terms and debates is enough to hold your own.

essentials.title: Large language models
essentials.body: Chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek run on large language models (LLMs): systems trained on huge amounts of text to predict and generate language.

essentials.title: Generative AI
essentials.body: AI that creates text, images, video, music and code. Tools like Midjourney and Sora make images and video from prompts.

essentials.title: Chips and compute
essentials.body: Training AI needs enormous computing power, mostly Nvidia chips in giant data centres. That's why Nvidia became the world's most valuable company.

essentials.title: The big labs
essentials.body: OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Meta and xAI in the US; DeepSeek, Alibaba (Qwen), Moonshot and others in China. They race to release better models.

essentials.title: Agents are the next step
essentials.body: AI 'agents' can take actions on their own, like browsing, coding or booking, not just answering questions.

essentials.title: Risks and rules
essentials.body: Concerns include misinformation, deepfakes, job loss, bias and long-term safety. The EU passed an AI Act; other countries are writing rules.

names.name: OpenAI
names.what: Maker of ChatGPT, the most-used AI chatbot. CEO Sam Altman.

names.name: Sam Altman
names.what: OpenAI's CEO and the face of the AI boom.

names.name: Google DeepMind
names.what: Google's AI lab behind Gemini; led by Nobel laureate Demis Hassabis.

names.name: Anthropic
names.what: Maker of Claude, founded by former OpenAI researchers with a focus on safety.

names.name: Nvidia / Jensen Huang
names.what: The chip maker powering AI, and its leather-jacketed CEO, born in Taiwan.

names.name: DeepSeek
names.what: Chinese lab whose cheap, powerful R1 model shocked markets in January 2025.

names.name: Meta
names.what: Facebook's parent, building Llama models and spending heavily on AI talent.

names.name: xAI / Grok
names.what: Elon Musk's AI company and its chatbot.

names.name: Microsoft
names.what: OpenAI's biggest backer, putting Copilot everywhere.

names.name: TSMC
names.what: Taiwan's chipmaker that manufactures most advanced AI chips.

names.name: Geoffrey Hinton
names.what: 'Godfather of AI', Nobel Prize winner who now warns about AI risks.

timeline.event: IBM's Deep Blue beats chess champion Garry Kasparov.
Deep learning breakthrough with neural networks on GPUs.
DeepMind's AlphaGo beats Go champion Lee Sedol.
Google researchers publish the Transformer, the basis of today's LLMs.
ChatGPT launches and reaches 100 million users in two months.
GPT-4, Claude and Gemini launch; AI investment explodes.
AI pioneers win Nobel Prizes in physics and chemistry.
DeepSeek shock; agents and reasoning models; Nvidia hits $5 trillion; GPT-5 launches.

now.headline: AI at work
now.detail: Companies push staff to use AI tools; people swap tips on what actually saves time.

now.headline: Jobs debate
now.detail: Entry-level white-collar jobs, coding and customer service are seen as most exposed.

now.headline: Bubble talk
now.detail: Hundreds of billions are being spent on data centres; investors debate whether returns will follow.

now.headline: US vs China
now.detail: Chip export controls and competing Chinese models make AI a geopolitical race.

now.headline: Coding agents
now.detail: AI tools that write and fix code have become one of the most-used AI products.

local.headline: Access in Hong Kong
local.detail: Some US AI services, including ChatGPT, don't officially serve Hong Kong. People use alternatives, workplace tools or Chinese models.

local.headline: Chinese AI popular
local.detail: DeepSeek, Qwen and Doubao are widely used locally and in the mainland.

local.headline: Government push
local.detail: Hong Kong is funding AI research and supercomputing at Cyberport as part of its tech hub ambitions.

local.headline: Deepfake scams
local.detail: In 2024 a Hong Kong company lost about HK$200 million after staff were tricked by a deepfake video call.

debates.question: Will AI take my job?
debates.sides: Optimists say it changes jobs rather than eliminating them; pessimists see big displacement.

debates.question: Is AI a bubble?
debates.sides: Real usage and revenue vs dot-com-style overinvestment.

debates.question: Open or closed models?
debates.sides: Open models spread innovation; closed models may be safer.

debates.question: Is AGI close?
debates.sides: Some leaders say within years; sceptics say decades or never.
